_comment: Block manifest graded by `klt signoff --manifest`. See README.md for the regeneration command and the pin.

ITEM 5 (full corner verification vs a ratified spec), added by issue #30. Five `klt sim` envelopes, one per row family, each naming the spec/target-spec.md row ids it covers; `spec_rows.5` declares the FULL row set, so a row no envelope covers is visible in the report instead of being silently absent.

The declared row set is spec/target-spec.md's ELECTRICAL rows -- the rows whose Binding-conditions column is the §PVT grid. The Area and Signoff rows of that table are deliberately NOT declared here: their binding conditions are a layout cell and the DRC/LVS/ERC decks, which T1 items 2, 3 and 4 grade. Declaring them under item 5 would make a layout artifact a corner-verification gap.

Item 5 is UNMET on purpose. Three declared rows are gaps: the untrimmed-line 3-sigma row, the trimmed-line row and the Trim row. The first needs a device-mismatch Monte Carlo reduction (issue #31), which a corner matrix cannot express and which T1 item 6 grades; the other two need a trim network that does not exist in this design yet. Naming a narrower row set would have rendered item 5 `met` by leaving the block's unevidenced accuracy rows out of the declaration, which is exactly the relaxation CLAUDE.md forbids.

The Supply row is declared as a gap rather than covered because spec/target-spec.md states it is met BY CONSTRUCTION (HV device rating, inherited) and not by a result: every cited envelope did run the ratified 2.97/3.30/3.63 V axis, but no measurement in them establishes the row, and asserting coverage from a supply value the request itself set would be circular.

Each cited envelope carries `spec_row` tags on its graded measurements, so `klt signoff` DERIVES this coverage from the envelopes (`row_coverage.row_sources` reads `derived`) instead of taking the manifest's word for it.

ITEM 6 (statistical claims carry Monte Carlo evidence), added by issue #31. One `klt yield` report, and `spec_rows.6` declaring the FULL statistical row set. spec/decision-records/0014-statistical-mc-sections-and-window.md records which rows are statistical and why, which model sections the campaign uses, and the window the report is graded against.

Item 6 is UNMET on purpose, and for a reason the evidence states rather than hides. `vref_untrimmed_line_3sigma` IS covered -- the campaign measures the row's quantity, with its seed, its sample size, its deterministic zero-spread control and a known-bad control that the statistics do detect -- but it is declared `ratified: false`, so `klt signoff` reports `partial_coverage` and never `met`. Two things are unratified about it: the limit the yield is graded against is an evidence-reporting window read out of the item-5 envelope, not a bound spec/target-spec.md ratifies (it ratifies none for this row), and the mechanism the row names is only partly reachable in this PDK -- resistor mismatch is sampled per instance, bipolar and MOS mismatch are not sampled at all, because pnpMPA has no per-instance mismatch model and the MOS one is gated on an instance parameter no `klt sim` request can set. Declaring the row `ratified: true` would assert a bound nobody ratified; declaring it a gap would hide a campaign that did run.

`vref_trimmed_line` is the second statistical row and is a declared gap: it needs a trim network this design does not contain. `trim` is deliberately NOT declared under item 6 -- spec/target-spec.md's Monte Carlo column says `no` for it, and its own evidence is a deterministic monotonicity sweep; what it takes from the Monte Carlo is the range it has to cover, not its own statistics. Record 0014 section 4 accounts for every spec row this way.

The item-6 citation DOES pin a content_hash, where the item-5 citations do not. The difference is what the hash would bind: a klt sim envelope's provenance.input hashes a per-corner deck generated under sim/build/ (gitignored), so a pin there would name a path no reviewer has. A klt yield report's freshness pin is the sample-set document its `samples` field names, and that document IS committed beside the report (...line.samples.json), carrying both populations and the sha256 of both source envelopes. So the pin is checkable from a clean checkout. Its one limit, stated by klt yield's own docs: klt signoff does not recursively re-hash the campaigns that document's `derivation` block names, so editing a source envelope without re-running sim/mc-yield.sh would leave the pin satisfied. sim/tests/test-mc-bench.sh re-checks that both named envelopes are committed, and the envelopes are append-only.

A grading outcome worth knowing before reading the report: item 6's detail lists vref_untrimmed_line_3sigma under `uncovered_rows` AS WELL AS `unratified_rows`, even though the citation above resolves and passes its campaign-discipline gates (sample size sufficient, negative control detected). klt signoff's item-6 row reader counts only a citation whose report `status` is `pass`, and a klt yield report that declares no `target_yield` is `status: "reported"` -- which is the correct state for a row that ratifies no yield claim. Declaring a target the campaign is known to clear would make the row read as covered; that would be manufacturing a claim to satisfy a grader, so it is not done. Filed generically as klayout-tools#5490. The item-6 verdict is `unmet` / `partial_coverage` either way.

ITEM 7 (post-layout verification), added by issue #32. ONE `klt pex` envelope, produced in `--extract-only` mode (klayout-tools#3739, closed in the 0.8.0 pin this record is graded at). It is cited and graded `unmet` / `check_failed` ON PURPOSE: the curated `sg13cmos5l` extraction deck declares no bipolar class, so the extracted `bandgap_top` netlist is missing all three `pnpMPA` devices of the core (17 devices against the design's 20 cards / 27 units) and no schematic-vs-extracted delta can be computed against it. Not citing it at all would render item 7 `no_evidence`, which would hide a run that did happen and does establish something -- a clean `parasitic_integrity` result, fully biased device bodies, and the lumped-RC model's own scope statement. Every spec row the item-5 benches grade is `insufficient-evidence` for item 7; no item-5 row and no ratified bound changes. See spec/decision-records/0012-post-layout-pex-extraction-gap.md and sim/pex-bandgap-top/README.md.

No `content_hash` is pinned on the item-7 citation, for the same reason item 5's are unpinned (README.md): what pins it is the record beside it, which carries the layout, extracted-netlist and schematic-DUT sha256s plus the device inventory, and sim/tests/test-pex-device-inventory.sh re-derives that inventory from the committed netlists on every CI run.

5.gap: device-mismatch Monte Carlo reduction (3 sigma over N >= 300 samples per corner point) that a klt sim corner matrix cannot express; it is T1 item 6's to grade, and item 6 now cites the campaign that measured it (sim/closed-loop-vref-mc, decision record 0014). Still a gap for item 5, which is corner verification
needs a trim network, which this design does not contain; spec/target-spec.md ratifies the method only, and the row is not stated as a number until measured
needs a trim network, which this design does not contain; spec/target-spec.md makes the Trim row conditional on the untrimmed Monte Carlo showing a trimmable offset

spec/target-spec.md records this row as met by construction (HV device rating, inherited), not by a result; every cited envelope ran the ratified 2.97/3.30/3.63 V axis, but no measurement establishes the row and asserting it from a supply the request itself set would be circular

6.note: Covered by the klt yield report cited above. Declared unratified because spec/target-spec.md states no number for this row (its Target column is a method) -- so the min/max the yield is computed against is the deterministic PVT envelope the item-5 bench measured, used as an evidence-reporting window and labelled as one in sim/closed-loop-vref-mc/yield-limits.json -- and because the device-mismatch mechanism the row names is only partly reachable at the pin (spec/decision-records/0014-statistical-mc-sections-and-window.md).

6.gap: needs a modelled 1-point trim at 27 C, i.e. a trim network this design does not contain; spec/target-spec.md ratifies the method only and says the row is not stated as a number until measured
